title: docs(console): FormPage's features comment points at the form-view refusal (objectui#6262)
body:
Fixes #6262

Clause-②: no

## What this does

objectui#6262 recorded a mismatch between routes. `/forms/:name` binds `features` to an empty map, so a `features.*` predicate on a form view faults there and `visibleWhen` fails open. Inside an app, the same text evaluates against the real flags. On 2026-08-27 the maintainer ruled **option B**: form-view predicates may not name the `features` root at all. objectstack-ai/objectstack#12665 (landed as objectstack PR 12849) put that refusal into `@objectstack/spec`, and the spec CHANGELOG lists it under **17.3.0**. This PR does the objectui half of the work, as triage listed it (comment 5816808429):

1. It measures the refusal at objectui's authoring door, with a positive control (see below).
2. It rewrites the `features` paragraph of `FormPage`'s predicate-scope comment. That paragraph said `features` is "empty here rather than fetched" and that wiring it would be "a different card". It now states the rule and records that fetching `/auth/config` was ruled out.
3. It adds a console pin, `apps/console/src/__tests__/formViewFeaturesRootRefused-6262.test.ts`, so the comment's claim is backed by a test that re-checks it.
4. It adds an empty-frontmatter changeset, `.changeset/6262-form-features-scope-refused.md`. Nothing is released.

Option A (fetching `/auth/config` on `/forms/:name`) is not revived. The renderer is unchanged.

## Measurement (premise A1)

The lockfile installs `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0**, and `apps/console` and `packages/app-shell` both load it from the same `.pnpm` path. The refusal is the `superRefine` on `FormViewSchema` (`checkFormViewPredicateFeaturesRoot`). `ViewItemSchema`, `ViewSchema` and `ViewMetadataSchema` each carry it into their form-view config.

**Through the real door.** A throwaway test called `validateMetadataDraft('view', body, undefined, { mode })` from `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.ts`. The body was the ExpandedViewItem envelope (`viewKind: 'form'`) that `/forms/:name` loads. The test was not committed: it was deleted after the run, and the tree was confirmed clean afterwards.

| mode | predicate site | target `features.multiOrgEnabled` | control `current_user.role == 'admin'` |
|---|---|---|---|
| create (`ViewItemSchema`) | field | refused at `config.sections.0.fields.0.visibleWhen` | ok, 0 issues |
| create | section | refused at `config.sections.0.visibleWhen` | ok, 0 issues |
| edit (`ViewMetadataSchema`) | field | refused at `config.sections.0.fields.0.visibleWhen` | ok, 0 issues |
| edit | section | refused at `config.sections.0.visibleWhen` | ok, 0 issues |

Every refusal has zod issue code `custom`, and its message begins "Form-view predicates may not name the `features.*` scope root (ruled 2026-08-27)." Parsing directly with `FormViewSchema`, `ViewItemSchema`, `ViewSchema` (the container's `form`) and `ViewMetadataSchema` gives the same result: all four refuse the target and accept the control. So the premise holds, and the restart condition on the card is met.

That reading is **one-time**. `@object-ui/app-shell` does not export `validateMetadataDraft`, so a pin that calls it would have to live in `packages/app-shell`, which is outside this claim's file surface. The committed pin (next section) parses the same two schemas the `view` gates use, and its header says what it does not cover.

I also checked whether objectui's own view editor suggests the `features` root for form-view predicates. It does not. `conditionScope.ts` rules `view: 'none'`, so those fields are a plain string input with no suggested roots.

## The pin

`formViewFeaturesRootRefused-6262.test.ts` has 8 tests. It covers 2 gates (`ViewItemSchema` for create, `ViewMetadataSchema` for edit) and 2 predicate sites (field and section). For each pair there are two tests:

- **Control:** the body must parse clean.
- **Target:** the body is refused with exactly one issue. The issue has code `custom`, sits at that predicate's path, and its message names `features.*`.

**Reverse verification** was one-time, run on committed `c8b893c63` with a trap that restores the file. It swapped `TARGET` to `record.features.multiOrgEnabled`, which is member access that the spec keeps legal. On disk, the new spelling appeared once and the old spelling zero times.

- Result: `Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8)`.
- All four target tests went red, with "expected true to be false" on `parsed.success`. All four controls stayed green, which is the expected direction.
- The restore was confirmed by a matching HEAD-blob hash (`c1f4c22b4`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- The later commit `a440581af` changed only the pin's header comment. The assertions were not touched.

## Verification at HEAD `a440581af`

**Tests.** I ran `pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=verbose` through the verify lock on three files: the pin, `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.viewShapes.test.ts`. Result: `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 28 passed (28)`.

**Gates**, all exit 0:

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: 2 source files of 1 released package, 1 changeset with empty frontmatter.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`.
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:spec-symbols` and `check:vi-mock-specifiers`.

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the 3 paths reports NOT GOVERNED. The PR stays draft anyway, because it came from a dispatch.

**Lint (declared narrowing: touched files only).** I ran `eslint --format json` in `apps/console` over the 2 lintable files.

- Result: 2 files, 0 errors. The new test has 0 warnings. `FormPage.tsx` has 21 warnings. Linting the base blob `6099dd870` gives the same 21 rules and messages. The only difference is the code-frame line numbers, which the longer comment shifts by 5.
- What the narrowing covers: console's `lint` script is `eslint .` over `apps/console`. The changeset is markdown and is not linted.
- Why the narrowing is safe: the printed config has no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off. This diff therefore cannot change the lint result of any file it did not touch.

**Type-check (declared narrowing).** Console's `type-check` needs the built `@object-ui/*` dist, and this fresh worktree has not built it.

- I checked the new test under console's own tsconfig (`extends ./tsconfig.json`, with `files` set to the test): exit 0, the file appears in `--listFiles`, 0 errors.
- Negative control: the same config plus a deliberately ill-typed file gives exit 2 with TS2322.
- `FormPage.tsx` changed only in comment text.
- The full console type-check is left to CI.

**Patch round 1:** merged `origin/main` `8b1f06619` and pushed head `954d5feaf`. `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` all exit 0; the pin passes 8/8.

## Acceptance notes

- **The stale clause in `.changeset/6038-production-predicate-fault-warning.md` is corrected** in `d57e8e5ed` (patch round 1, prose only, frontmatter untouched). It now reads: the `features` root on `/forms/:name`, which objectui#6262 settled by refusing it in form-view predicates rather than wiring it.
- `FormPage.tsx` also contains an older claim about the installed spec version ("measured against the installed 17.0.0", in the `FormViewBody` note). The `check:installed-pin-claims` ledger already records it as `stale`. It is outside the `features` block, so I did not touch it.
- All 8 comments on the card were readable from this seat over REST. Triage's note said that one of the 7 comments at that time was not readable by it.
